The Origin

Born of Gods, Forged in War

The Greatest Warrior of All Greece

Achilles, the swift-footed son of King Peleus of Phthia and the sea goddess Thetis, was destined from birth to become the mightiest warrior the world had ever known. His mother, seeking to make him invulnerable, dipped him in the River Styx — but held him by his heel, leaving one mortal weakness.

Raised by the centaur Chiron on Mount Pelion, Achilles was trained in the arts of war, music, medicine, and the hunt. When the call came for the expedition against Troy, he sailed with a thousand ships, knowing the prophecy — that he would die young but achieve eternal glory.

The Legend

Chronicle of a Hero

Chapter I

The River Styx

Thetis dips the infant Achilles into the River Styx, making his body invulnerable — save for the heel by which she held him. This single weakness would echo through eternity.

Chapter II

Training on Mount Pelion

The centaur Chiron educates young Achilles in warfare, healing, and the arts. He grows into the fastest, strongest warrior Greece has ever seen, mastering the spear, sword, and shield.

Chapter III

The Trojan War Begins

Helen of Sparta is taken to Troy. A thousand ships set sail. Achilles, though knowing his fate — glory and an early death — leads the Myrmidons across the sea to the shores of Ilium.

Chapter IV

Wrath of Achilles

When Agamemnon dishonors him by seizing Briseis, Achilles withdraws from battle. The Greeks suffer devastating losses without their greatest champion on the field.

Chapter V

The Death of Patroclus

Patroclus, beloved companion of Achilles, dons his armor and enters battle — only to be slain by Hector. Consumed by grief and rage, Achilles returns to the battlefield with a fury the world has never seen.

Chapter VI

The Slaying of Hector

Achilles hunts Hector across the walls of Troy three times before confronting him in single combat. With his divine spear, he slays the Trojan prince and drags his body behind his chariot.

Chapter VII

The Fall of the Hero

At the Scaean Gates, Paris — guided by the god Apollo — looses an arrow that strikes Achilles in his only vulnerable spot: his heel. The greatest warrior falls, but his name becomes eternal.

The Arsenal

Weapons of Legend

🗡️

The Spear of Pelion

A massive spear of ash from Mount Pelion, gifted by Chiron. So heavy that only Achilles could wield it in battle, it was said to have been used to slay countless warriors, including Hector of Troy.

🛡️

Shield of Achilles

When his original armor was lost, the god Hephaestus forged a new shield depicting the heavens, the earth, the sea, cities at war and at peace — a microcosm of the entire world in divine bronze and gold.

⚔️

Xiphos & Armor

His complete panoply included a gleaming bronze helmet with a golden crest, corselet, and greaves — all crafted by the gods. Even without his legendary spear, Achilles was unmatched in close combat.

An Eternal Legacy

For over three thousand years, the name Achilles has echoed through the corridors of human memory. He is more than a mythological figure — he is the archetype of the hero who chooses glory over length of days, who burns so brightly that his light can never be extinguished.

His story, immortalized by Homer in the Iliad, has inspired countless works of art, literature, and film. From ancient Greek amphorae to modern cinema, the tale of the swift-footed warrior continues to captivate hearts across the world.

The concept of an "Achilles heel" — a single fatal weakness in an otherwise invincible entity — has become one of the most enduring metaphors in human language.

"Sing, O goddess, the anger of Achilles son of Peleus, that brought countless ills upon the Achaeans..."

— Homer, The Iliad, Book I
